interface_notes.value: In the α (BCC) phase the lattice parameter of the κ phase is 0.387–0.389 nm and α/κ interfaces are semicoherent (lattice mismatch 6% [59]); in the ferritic matrix κ-carbides are present as semicoherent precipitates with thick, elongated rod-like shape, in contrast to the nanoscale cuboidal coherent κ-carbides found in austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels.

phase_evolution.value: In the ferritic Fe-Al matrix the δ-ferrite is directly produced from liquid; there is no γ↔α transformation over the process temperature range, so the ferrite matrix is retained through cold rolling and annealing while κ-carbides may precipitate.

processing_steps_notes.value: Cold rolling is a necessary step to change the grain structure, grain size and texture in ferritic low density steels; a fully recrystallized microstructure can be obtained after final recrystallization annealing following a 50% cold rolling reduction in a Fe-7%Al steel [41].

source.reason: b0114 states cold rolling and annealing are necessary steps for ferritic low density steels and that a 50% cold rolling reduction in a Fe-7%Al steel precedes recrystallization annealing.

processing_steps_notes.value: The ferritic Fe-Al steels are generally cold rolled and heated to 700–1000 °C for recrystallization annealing to control the grain size and texture of the ferrite matrix as well as the precipitation of κ-carbides, applying the continuous annealing line used for conventional HSLA steel strips (b0105). A fully recrystallized microstructure is obtained after final recrystallization annealing within 700–950 °C following a 50% cold rolling reduction in a Fe-7%Al steel (b0114).

overall_structure.value: Single-phase δ-ferrite matrix, fully recrystallized after cold rolling plus recrystallization annealing; δ-ferrite grains become more or less equiaxed with a random texture (relatively higher intensity of the Cube fibre). As Al not only extends the ferrite region to high temperatures but also raises the recrystallization temperature of ferrite, the δ-ferrite grain size cannot be sufficiently refined during hot rolling, so cold rolling and annealing are required; the δ-ferrite is the phase directly produced from the liquid.
